Subject: Redwood as 'Service Provider' under CPRA + subprocessor list request

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Acme Health's clinical ops team was impressed with the latency and the prefix caching examples. Before we move to procurement, legal/Privacy had a couple of gating items:

1) They want explicit confirmation that Redwood will act as a "service provider" (i.e., processor equivalent) under CPRA/CCPA and will not "sell" personal data.
2) We need a current subprocessor inventory (names, locations, purpose) and whether any subprocessors will process California sensitive categories.
3) Any constraints on cross-border transfers (we have some ROIs outside the US).

Can you send the addendum language you propose and the subprocessor spreadsheet? If you already have SOC2 evidence or a short attestation, that would speed review.

Would appreciate a response by EOD Monday 5/4 so Procurement can calendar the contract review.

Best,
Alex

Vanessa / Jasmine — quick answers and suggested language below. Kept it short since Acme wants vendor-provided text: 

1) Service provider / no-sale confirmation (short clause to include in the US-state privacy addendum):
"Redwood Inference ("Provider") acts as a service provider on behalf of Customer under applicable California privacy law (including the CCPA/CPRA). Provider will process Personal Information solely for the business purposes directed by Customer and will not sell Personal Information as defined under California law."

2) Subprocessor inventory: Jasmine, please attach the master sheet (include locations and purpose). We should redact internal contact emails but include country and whether the subprocessors may access California-sensitive categories.

3) Cross-border transfers: Our standard approach — data remains in US regions by default for this offering; where customers opt into multi-region hosting, we use contractual safeguards and documented subprocessors in those regions. Suggest adding this language: 
"Provider will not transfer Personal Information outside the United States except as necessary to provide the Services. Where transfers occur, Provider will maintain appropriate contractual safeguards and subprocessors' information will be disclosed to Customer."

4) Attestations / evidence: Attach SOC2 Type II summary and offer an executive SOC2 attestation letter. If Acme requires full report, coordinate NDA with Security.

Action items: Jasmine to attach spreadsheet + SOC2 summary; Vanessa to send vendor-proposed addendum + attachments to Alex and Maria. If Security flags anything unusual (e.g., decryption by subprocessor), escalate.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Hi Alex / Maria — thanks for the quick follow-up. Please find below the vendor-proposed addendum language and the requested materials. We aimed to be explicit about the "service provider" role and give a clear path for Acme's procurement/legal review.

1) Addendum excerpt (vendor-proposed):
"Redwood Inference ("Provider") performs its services as a Service Provider under the CCPA/CPRA and equivalent state privacy laws. Provider processes Personal Information only on behalf of Customer and in accordance with Customer's documented instructions. Provider does not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information for any purposes unrelated to the performance of the Services and will not sell Personal Information as defined under California law. Provider will enter into reasonably necessary subprocessor agreements and remain responsible for acts and omissions of its subprocessors."

2) Subprocessors inventory: attached (see column 'CustomerDisclosure' for entries we recommend disclosing to Acme; Belgium and India are flagged). If you need US-only hosting, we can provide a DPA variant that restricts processing to US regions only and lists only US-based subprocessors.

3) SOC2 evidence: attached is the SOC2 Type II summary. For the full report, we can provide access under an NDA or via secure share.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether this language meets your requirements or whether you want us to provide an alternative US-only addendum.
- If you want the full SOC2 report, let us know and we'll route the NDA.
- If Acme requires any contractual limitation on subprocessors or a right to object to new subprocessors, we can propose defined objection windows (e.g., 10 business days) in the addendum.

Happy to hop on a quick call with Maria and Procurement if that helps resolve items faster.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
